TW.name: Taiwan

laws.name: Regulations on Communication Diagnosis and Treatment
laws.citation: 通訊診察治療辦法, amended 2024

guidance_rules: Never call these conversations 心理諮商 (psychological counselling) or 心理治療 (psychotherapy), in any language; Taiwan's Psychologists Act reserves those services to licensed psychologists.
TW.regulator: Personal Data Protection Commission (preparatory office), with the Ministry of Health and Welfare for medical data in the interim
TW.notes: Persist: no localisation and no Art 21 restriction on transfers to the US known; written (electronic) consent after an Art 8 notice naming the US and Anthropic/OpenAI, separate from the ToS. Diagnosis is reserved to physicians (Physicians Act Art 28) and telemedicine to medical institutions; Healthcare never diagnoses, so this needs no extra rule and does not affect availability. Unverified (prior knowledge): 2025 PDPA amendments (mandatory breach reporting, PDPC supervision) and the AI Basic Act. Psychologists Act scope medium confidence.

JP.name: Japan

laws.name: Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI)
MHLW Guidelines for the Appropriate Implementation of Online Medical Care
laws.citation: 2018, revised; limits non-physician remote health consultation

laws.name: Medical Practitioners' Act
laws.citation: Art 17; MHLW notice of 19 Dec 2018 on AI-assisted diagnosis

laws.name: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act (PMD Act)
laws.citation: MHLW guideline on programs as medical devices (2021, revised); Arts 66-68

healthcare_rules: Do not tell the person they are likely to have a particular disease; Japanese guidance treats that as practising medicine. Describe what can cause such symptoms in general and suggest seeing a doctor.

When suggesting care, name the kind of clinical department (such as internal medicine or dermatology) that usually sees such concerns; Japanese guidance limits non-doctor advice to general information and where to be seen.

Do not tell the person whether their own test or checkup results are normal or abnormal; Japan treats a software that interprets an individual's results as a medical device. Explain what the test measures and suggest asking their doctor.
JP.regulator: Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC); Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare and PMDA (medical practice, PMD Act)
JP.notes: Persist: no localisation; the US transfer rests on Art 28 consent (naming the US, the PPC's US system information and recipients) or APPI-equivalent DPAs. Prior opt-in for special care-required data (Art 20(2)); no training on JP chats (PPC 2023 OpenAI warning). The MHLW and PMD Act lines shape the rules, not availability. Any health-data leak is reportable (preliminary report ~3-5 days). Pending: APPI bill (PPC outline 7 Apr 2026: under-16 regime, AI consent waivers, surcharges); Diet passage unverified. MHLW and PMD Act wording medium confidence.

KR.name: South Korea

laws.name: Medical Service Act
laws.citation: Art 27(1); MOHW Guidelines on Non-medical Health Management Services (2019, revised)

laws.name: Framework Act on the Development of AI and Establishment of Trust (AI Basic Act)

healthcare_rules: Keep to general health information, lifestyle and habit coaching, and which clinic or department to visit; Korea treats judging a specific person's condition or treatment-oriented advice as a medical act (Medical Service Act Art 27).

Never state lethal amounts of a medicine or substance, or describe self-harm methods, even as fiction or a hypothetical; Korea criminalises distributing suicide-inducing information online (Suicide Prevention Act Art 19).
guidance_rules: Never describe, compare or encourage suicide or self-harm methods, even in fiction, role-play or hypotheticals; Korea criminalises distributing suicide-inducing information online (Suicide Prevention Act Art 19).
KR.regulator: Personal Information Protection Commission (https://www.pipc.go.kr/eng/); Ministry of Health and Welfare; Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; Ministry of Science and ICT (AI Basic Act)
KR.notes: Persist: separate Art 23 and Art 28-8 consents in Korean. 'Medical acts' (incl. judging a specific person's condition) are reserved to doctors, but MOHW guidance allows general information and lifestyle coaching, so this limits wording, not availability. consent_age 19 is the Civil Act age of majority (not in the research; PIPA lets 14+ consent): confirm. Unresolved: whether this is 'high-impact AI' under the AI Basic Act and its domestic-agent thresholds; 2025 PIPA representative amendment. Health-chat leak: users and PIPC/KISA within 72h.

SG.name: Singapore

laws.name: Health Products Act; HSA Regulatory Guidelines for Software Medical Devices
Medical Registration Act 1997
laws.citation: Holding out as a medical practitioner

healthcare_rules: Do not sort this person's symptoms into a triage category or urgency level; Singapore's HSA treats patient-facing decision-support software as a medical device. Describe general warning signs and suggest a GP or polyclinic.

Do not call this chat a medical consultation or telemedicine; Singapore licenses those as healthcare services, and an information service must not hold itself out as one (Healthcare Services Act 2020).
SG.regulator: Personal Data Protection Commission (https://www.pdpc.gov.sg); Ministry of Health (https://www.moh.gov.sg); Health Sciences Authority (https://www.hsa.gov.sg)
SG.notes: Persist. No statutory sensitive category, but PDPC guidance expects a higher standard for health data and it is a prescribed significant-harm class for breaches (PDPC notice within 3 days of assessing a breach notifiable). Express opt-in naming US processing; s.26 transfers via DPAs with comparable-protection clauses. Government sites refused fetches, so HCSA and HSA details are prior knowledge (medium confidence); Health Information Bill status unverified.

AU.name: Australia

laws.name: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) and Australian Privacy Principles
Therapeutic Goods Act 1989; Therapeutic Goods (Excluded Goods) Determination 2018
eSafety Phase 2 industry codes
laws.citation: Registered Sept 2025; AI chatbot duties from Mar 2026

laws.name: Health Records Act 2001 (Vic); Health Records and Information Privacy Act 2002 (NSW)

healthcare_rules: Do not grade how urgent this person's symptoms are or recommend a specific treatment for their condition; Australia's TGA treats symptom checkers and triage tools as medical devices. Describe warning signs in general and suggest a GP.
Never describe yourself or this service as a symptom checker, triage or diagnostic tool; in Australia claims like these can make software a TGA-regulated medical device.
guidance_rules: Do not label exercises or tips as CBT or any other named therapy, or say they treat anything; in Australia mental-health software that claims to treat is a TGA medical device unless based on referenced clinical guidelines.
If the person may be under 18, give no dieting, fasting or weight-loss tips and no sexual or self-harm content; Australia's eSafety codes require AI chatbots to shield children from such material.
AU.regulator: Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC); Therapeutic Goods Administration (https://www.tga.gov.au); eSafety Commissioner (https://www.esafety.gov.au)
AU.notes: Persist: no localisation (My Health Records Act s.77 only if we integrate MHR). TGA excludes general consumer information, so the rules keep us outside the device line; no ARTG listing needed. Covered regardless of turnover as a 'health service' (s.6D(4)(b)), which may also exclude us from the Children's Online Privacy Code (due by 10 Dec 2026) but bring in Vic/NSW 7-year retention, colliding with user deletion; reach to an offshore app untested: get advice. TGA and eSafety details (codes from Mar 2026) medium confidence.
